summary.en: Store related values in indexed elements and keep every access inside the array.
summary.bn: একই ধরনের অনেক মান ইনডেক্স দিয়ে রাখো; অ্যারের সীমার ভেতরে থেকে পড়া ও লেখা শেখো।

notes: Fixed arrays work in C89; designated initializers such as [2] = 7 need C99.

sections.title: Keep related values under one name
C does not check each index for you
Separate an element count from an index
Keep capacity and used length visible
Use an index within a known range

examples.title: Initialize, read and replace marks
examples.explanationHtml: Index 1 selects the second mark, which becomes 75. The loop visits exactly indices 0 through 3.

examples.title: Compare array initializer forms
examples.explanationHtml: The inferred array has three elements. Omitted elements in partial and selected are initialized to zero.

examples.title: Compute the element count without assuming int size
examples.explanationHtml: The quotient is 5 regardless of how many bytes this implementation uses per int. rolls is still an actual array here.

practice.title: Read and echo a bounded array
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 10, then n ints from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: before input, then the values separated by spaces and a final newline. For zero, print an empty line.
hints: The echo loop uses i < n.

practice.title: Change one indexed value
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 1 to 10 and n ints from -100 to 100, then index and replacement. Index is from 0 to n-1 and replacement from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: first, then Index and replacement: before the extra pair, then the changed array.
hints: Validate the index before assigning the element.

practice.title: Sum alternate positions
practice.statementHtml: For the indexed-position task, read a length n from 0 to 20, then n integers in [-100, 100]. Print Count and values: first, then the sum at indices 0, 2, 4 and so on.
hints: An index is a position, not the value stored there.

practice.title: Compare the endpoint elements
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 1 to 20 and n ints from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: then Same when the first and last values match, or Different otherwise.
hints: The last index is n - 1 even for a one-element array.

quiz.prompt: What is the final valid index of int marks[6]?
quiz.explanation: Six elements occupy positions zero through five.

options: Only the first element; the rest indeterminate
No elements until the first loop
quiz.explanation: A partial aggregate initializer zero-initializes every omitted element.

quiz.prompt: Updating index one changes which printed element?
quiz.explanation: Index one is the second element; the endpoints remain unchanged.

quiz.prompt: What is known about elements of an uninitialized automatic int array?
options: They retain values from the last program run
They all equal the array size
quiz.explanation: Automatic storage does not receive aggregate zero initialization without the relevant initialization rule.

quiz.prompt: Which expression counts elements when values is an actual array?
quiz.explanation: Dividing total bytes by element bytes gives the element count while the actual array type is available.

quiz.prompt: A partial initializer supplies only two values. What is a[3]?
quiz.explanation: The remaining two elements are zero-initialized.

quiz.prompt: Does int values[10] grow when code writes values[10]?
options: No, that element access is out of bounds
Only with a positive stored value
quiz.explanation: A fixed array retains its extent. Index ten is past the ten elements.

quiz.prompt: Which fact is portable about consecutive int array elements?
options: Every int is exactly four bytes
They have one padding byte between elements
Their addresses must be printed as decimal ints
quiz.explanation: Element width depends on the implementation, but array elements are consecutive complete elements.

quiz.prompt: A designated initializer selects index two. Which complete sequence appears?
quiz.explanation: Index two receives six; all other aggregate elements become zero.

quiz.prompt: Can a zero logical input length be represented with positive fixed capacity?
options: No, every array must be completely filled
Yes, set the used count to zero and access no elements
quiz.explanation: Logical length can be zero even though the reserved array has positive capacity.

keyPoints.en: An array stores consecutive elements of one element type.
keyPoints.bn: অ্যারে একই টাইপের উপাদান পরপর রাখে।

keyPoints.en: An array of n elements uses indices zero through n minus one.
keyPoints.bn: n উপাদানের অ্যারেতে ইনডেক্স শূন্য থেকে n-1 পর্যন্ত।

keyPoints.en: A partial initializer zero-initializes remaining elements.
keyPoints.bn: কিছু মান দিয়ে শুরু করলে বাকি উপাদানগুলো শূন্য হয়।

keyPoints.en: Uninitialized automatic array elements have indeterminate values.
keyPoints.bn: ইনিশিয়ালাইজ না করা অটোমেটিক অ্যারের উপাদানের মান অনির্ধারিত থাকে।

keyPoints.en: C does not automatically check an array index against its bounds.
keyPoints.bn: C নিজে থেকে ইনডেক্স অ্যারের সীমায় আছে কি না দেখে না।

keyPoints.en: sizeof an actual array gives the byte size of all its elements.
keyPoints.bn: আসল অ্যারের sizeof সব উপাদানের মোট বাইটসংখ্যা দেয়।

examQuestions.question: Explain valid indices, partial initialization and element counting for int a[4] = {7}.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The valid indices are zero through three. The first element is seven and the remaining elements are zero-initialized. While a is the actual array, sizeof a divided by sizeof a[0] gives four without assuming any particular int width. Index four is already outside the array.

#include <stdio.h>



int main(void)
{
    int a[3] = {4, 5, 6};
    a[1] = 9;
    printf("%d %d %d\n", a[0], a[1], a[2]);
    return 0;
}

4 9 6

Index one is the second element; the endpoints remain unchanged.

examQuestions.question: Read n from 1 to 20 and n ints from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: then Same when the first and last values match, or Different otherwise.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>



int main(void)
{
    int n;
    int values[20];
    puts("Count and values:");
    if (scanf("%d", &n) != 1 || n < 1 || n > 20) {
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (scanf("%d", &values[i]) != 1 || values[i] < -100 || values[i] > 100) {
            return 1;
        }
    }

    puts(values[0] == values[n - 1] ? "Same" : "Different");
    return 0;
}

The last index is n - 1 even for a one-element array.

For input 1 8, the program prints:

Count and values:
Same
